open_points.subject: State 1 authority for State 2
open_points.text: “The state is not yet closed by question rounds” conflicts with State 2 treating M01–M11 as normative and accepted dependencies.
open_points.question: Are all State 1 model statements authoritative for implementing State 2 despite State 1 not being closed?
options: Treat the current State 1 text as normative
Treat only owner-accepted portions as normative
Do not continue until State 1 is closed
open_points.default_guess: Treat the current State 1 text as normative because State 2 repeatedly relies on it.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession state
open_points.text: M11 says its complete facts are “its identity… the instant it began; its expiry”, while A13 requires a moving idle deadline, CSRF state and one-time confirmation values kept in the session.
open_points.question: Where are the last owner-request time, CSRF state and outstanding confirmation values represented, and are they facts of OwnerSession?
options: Add them as mutable OwnerSession facts
Keep them as separate runtime session state
Derive them without storing additional state
open_points.default_guess: Keep them as mutable runtime state attached to OwnerSession and amend the model accordingly.

open_points.subject: Confirmation-value consumption
open_points.text: A13 says a confirmation value “is used up by the first submission, whatever its answer”, but does not define whether a request failing session authentication, CSRF, parsing or confirmation lookup counts as that submission.
open_points.question: At which check is a confirmation value consumed, and which earlier failures leave it unused?
options: Consume once the value is found in its valid owner session
Consume before CSRF and action validation
Consume only after authentication and CSRF pass
open_points.default_guess: Consume it after the owner session and CSRF checks pass and the value is found, but before action-specific checks.

open_points.subject: Concurrent revocation, ending and agent calls
open_points.text: A10 says the check is made “at every call” and revocation holds “from the next call on”, without defining the result of a call concurrent with revocation, session ending or project erasure.
open_points.question: What event determines whether an in-flight agent call is before or after an access removal?
options: Call-start time
Transaction/check linearization point
Commit order
open_points.default_guess: Serialize the call with the access change and use the transaction's authorization-check linearization point.

open_points.subject: Answering a request for an already granted project
open_points.text: A12 says answering the request clears it and moves the version, M09 says an answer that grants writes a grant entry, while A05 says granting an already granted project writes no entry.
open_points.question: If a pending request is answered by granting a project already in the set, does clearing the request write a grant audit entry?
options: Write a grant entry because the combined action changed the pending request
Write no entry because the granted set did not change
Refuse this form of answer
open_points.default_guess: Move the access version for clearing the request but write no grant entry because no grant changed.

open_points.subject: Audit-entry existence invariant
open_points.text: A14 states “entry e exists <=> accepted action a with changed(a)”, while A15 later permits that entry to be erased by date.
open_points.question: Is A14's biconditional meant only at the transaction that performs the change, or must historical accepted changes always retain entries?
options: Limit the invariant to entry creation and retention until a later A15 erasure
Retain an immutable tombstone after audit erasure
Do not permit erasing entries created under A14
open_points.default_guess: Limit the biconditional to creation and qualify it with later erasure under A15.

open_points.subject: Durable audit sequence counter
open_points.text: A15 introduces “that last number durably, apart from the entries”, but State 1 says the listed models and facts are all Registry facts and declares no audit-counter model.
open_points.question: What model or store metadata owns the durable last-issued audit sequence number?
options: Add a singleton audit-counter model
Add it to migration/store metadata outside the domain models
Derive it from retained entries and allow reset when none remain
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit singleton store-metadata fact that is backed up with the store.

open_points.subject: Concurrent audit erasure and entry creation
open_points.text: A15 requires that after erase(d) “no entry with instant < start_of(d) remains”, but does not order the erasure transaction against a concurrent state change writing an audit entry.
open_points.question: How are audit erasure and concurrent audit-entry creation serialized, especially across the UTC date boundary?
options: Serialize every audit append with audit erasure
Use transaction commit order
Allow a concurrent qualifying entry to survive
open_points.default_guess: Serialize audit erasure with every audit append in one total log order.

open_points.subject: Import identifier namespace
open_points.text: A16 calls a record malformed when “an id occurs twice in the file” and checks conflicts for project, room, pointer and customer identifiers, without saying whether equality across different model kinds is a duplicate or conflict.
open_points.question: Are identifiers globally unique across all imported model kinds, or unique only within each kind?
options: One global identifier namespace
Separate namespace per model kind
Global for project, room and pointer but separate for customer
open_points.default_guess: Use separate namespaces per model kind unless the specification explicitly declares one global namespace.

open_points.subject: Imported withdrawn pointers
open_points.text: A16 accepts any pointer status in the vocabulary, including `withdrawn`, while M05 says an imported pointer “is never imported `withdrawn`”.
open_points.question: Must an import reject a pointer whose status is `withdrawn`?
options: Reject imported withdrawn pointers
Accept them with complete withdrawal facts
Accept them without withdrawal facts
open_points.default_guess: Reject them to follow M05.

open_points.subject: Import lifecycle consistency
open_points.text: A16 checks status vocabulary, pointer versions and readable instants but is silent on required relationships between status, marks and instants.
open_points.question: Which cross-field states are malformed, such as an active project with an archived instant, an archived project without one, or a superseded pointer without a superseded instant?
options: Validate every State 1 lifecycle invariant during import
Validate only the conditions explicitly listed in A16
Normalize inconsistent imported records
open_points.default_guess: Reject every imported record that violates a State 1 lifecycle invariant.

open_points.subject: Registry-minted customer references in import
open_points.text: A16 checks conflicts for “a Registry-minted `customer_ref`”, but neither it nor the identity format explains how imported data proves that a value was minted by Registry rather than being a v1 caller value.
open_points.question: How does Registry classify an imported customer reference as Registry-minted?
options: An explicit provenance field in the import format
Recognition by identifier syntax
Treat every VPS v1 value as non-minted
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit provenance field, while treating the known v1 source values as non-minted.

open_points.subject: Import file digest
open_points.text: A16 binds mapping, confirmation, closure and audit to “the file's digest” without declaring the digest algorithm or whether it covers the exact uploaded bytes or a canonical parsed representation.
open_points.question: How is the import digest computed?
options: Cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
Digest of a canonicalized parsed document
Algorithm and representation selected by each release
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-declared SHA-256 digest of the exact uploaded bytes.

open_points.subject: Uploaded import-file lifetime
open_points.text: A16 requires a confirmation to apply the exact file named by a prior digest and tests that uploading another file does not replace it, but says nothing about where uploaded files live or when they expire or are removed.
open_points.question: How long are unconfirmed upload bytes retained, and what happens after session expiry, restart, refusal, successful import or multiple uploads?
options: Retain per owner session until confirmation or session end
Persist by digest until explicit cleanup
Require re-upload at confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Retain each upload only in its owner session until confirmation, expiry, restart or successful use, then remove it.

open_points.subject: Restore-test service tokens
open_points.text: A18 requires the restored temporary instance to be “configured with no service token” and to start under A17, while A17 says every A09 service token is mandatory and a missing token stops the start.
open_points.question: How can the restore-test instance start without service tokens?
options: Define a restore-test startup mode exempt from the token requirement
Configure unreachable temporary tokens
Require all production service tokens in the restore instance
open_points.default_guess: Configure distinct temporary tokens and keep the instance unreachable.

open_points.subject: Backup encryption format
open_points.text: A18 says each backup is “encrypted with the backup key” but declares no authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce rules, format version or integrity failure behavior.
open_points.question: What exact encryption and authentication contract must every backup use?
options: A specified versioned AEAD backup format
Release-selected encryption recorded in each backup
Disk encryption alone
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD format with a fresh random nonce and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: Backup retention bound
open_points.text: A18 deletes old backups only “after a backup is written” and only when older than 30 days, yet promises that erased values disappear “at most 30 days after the erasure”. Failed backups or daily boundary timing can retain them for more than 30 days.
open_points.question: What process enforces the 30-day deletion deadline when a backup fails or when a backup reaches exactly 30 days between daily runs?
options: Run retention cleanup independently of backup success
Delete at age greater than or equal to 30 days before each run
Relax the bound to the next successful daily run
open_points.default_guess: Run cleanup independently every day and delete at age greater than or equal to 30 days.

open_points.subject: Backup recovery-point claim
open_points.text: A18 retries a failed backup only at the next 03:00 and keeps serving, while its consequence promises “at most a day of changes lost”. Repeated failures make the latest usable backup older than one day.
open_points.question: Is one day a guaranteed maximum recovery-point loss, or only the target when daily backups succeed?
options: Stop serving or block writes once the RPO would exceed one day
Describe one day as a monitored target rather than a guarantee
Retry within the day until a backup succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Retry during the day and treat an RPO beyond one day as an operational failure that must prevent an unqualified guarantee.

open_points.subject: Release restore-test version
open_points.text: A18 says “before each release” the latest backup is restored and the instance starts under A17, while A17 refuses a store whose version differs from the running release.
open_points.question: Is the restore test run with the old release, the candidate release before migration, or the candidate release after its store migration step?
options: Test restoration with the currently deployed release
Migrate the restored store and test with the candidate release
Run both tests
open_points.default_guess: Run both: prove the backup restores under the current release, then prove the release migration and candidate startup.

open_points.subject: Restored authorization and protection state
open_points.text: A18 says restore “loses every change made after the backup's instant” and only requires erasures to be repeated. This can resurrect ended sessions, revoked grants, archived projects, or pre-restriction customer data access, contradicting A10, A11, R0-46 and R0-65.
open_points.question: Which post-backup security and lifecycle changes must be replayed before a restored production instance serves?
options: Replay all accepted changes after the backup
Replay a declared safety-critical subset
Accept rollback of every non-erasure change
open_points.default_guess: Do not serve until every post-backup access revocation, session end, restriction, archive and erasure has been reconciled from an external recovery record.

open_points.subject: Migration closure after restore
open_points.text: A16 says the first successful import permanently closes import, while A18 permits restoring a backup from before the closure and instructs the owner to replay only erasures.
open_points.question: How is a successful migration closure preserved or restored so that a pre-import backup cannot reopen the one-time import?
options: Keep closure evidence outside the backed-up store
Replay the closure during recovery
Forbid restoring any backup predating the closure
open_points.default_guess: Keep independently recoverable closure evidence and restore it before serving.

open_points.subject: Audit sequence after restore
open_points.text: M09 and A15 say an audit sequence number is never reused, while A18 permits restoring an older counter and losing entries written after that backup.
open_points.question: How is the global audit high-water mark recovered so new entries do not reuse numbers issued after the backup?
options: Persist the high-water mark outside the backup cycle
Allow gaps but recover the maximum from an external record
Scope never-reused only to the current restored history
open_points.default_guess: Persist and recover the high-water mark independently before accepting writes.

open_points.subject: Backup-key replacement
open_points.text: A17 allows configuration changes at restart and holds only one backup key, while A18 requires old backups to remain readable for 30 days.
open_points.question: What happens to existing backups when the backup key changes?
options: Retain old keys until their backups expire
Re-encrypt every retained backup during rotation
Forbid key changes while retained backups use the old key
open_points.default_guess: Retain versioned old keys until every backup encrypted with them expires.

open_points.subject: Dependency digest definition
open_points.text: A20 requires the digest of every distribution and base image but does not declare the digest algorithm, canonical notation or treatment of a package available through several distribution files.
open_points.question: What exact artifact and digest must the release lock for each dependency?
options: Lock the exact distribution file and a specified cryptographic digest
Lock only package name and version plus any repository digest
Let the build system choose the digest format
open_points.default_guess: Lock the exact consumed artifact bytes with a release-wide SHA-256 digest format.

open_points.subject: Security-review category set
open_points.text: A21 says “Every security category has exactly one outcome below” but never defines the complete set of security categories against which completeness can be checked.
open_points.question: What authoritative taxonomy determines that no security category is missing from the review?
options: Declare a fixed taxonomy in the specification
Reference an external versioned taxonomy
Limit the claim to the categories explicitly listed
open_points.default_guess: Limit the current claim to the listed categories unless a versioned taxonomy is declared.

open_points.subject: Request-id collision across authorization scopes
open_points.text: A01 makes request ids unique only per model and says a differing collision is refused and “the caller reads the record”, without restricting lookup or disclosure to the stored record's project or principal.
open_points.question: What happens when Kernel supplies a request id already stored on a room or pointer belonging to another project or session?
options: Scope request ids by model and project or principal
Perform global lookup but return no stored record unless separately authorized
Use one global namespace and expose the collision record
open_points.default_guess: Use global deduplication per model but never disclose or return a stored record until authorization is checked against that record's actual project.

open_points.subject: Publish retry after artifact-type removal
open_points.text: A01 says no create precondition other than rights and archived-project checks is repeated and a publish retry returns its pointer, while A22 says publishing a removed type is refused as unknown.
open_points.question: Does a same-request-id retry of an earlier publish succeed after its artifact type has been removed from the release vocabulary?
options: Return the existing pointer as a replay
Refuse it as an unknown type
Return it only while the pointer remains published
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing pointer as a replay if the session and project checks still pass.

open_points.subject: Blank and whitespace-only values
open_points.text: A02 defines missing as `strip(v) = ""` but does not define the Unicode whitespace set or normalization used by `strip`.
open_points.question: Which code points count as whitespace for required and optional textual values?
options: Unicode White_Space property
ASCII whitespace only
The implementation language's native trim behavior
open_points.default_guess: Use the versioned Unicode White_Space property without normalizing nonblank text.

open_points.subject: Revision postcondition for erasure
open_points.text: A04 says every changed Project or Customer ends with `revision' = revision + 1`, while M01 and M04 say anonymisation or erasure removes the revision, and whole project deletion removes the record.
open_points.question: What does moving the revision mean for a transition whose result has no revision or no record?
options: Check the old revision but do not define a stored next revision
Increment transiently and record the resulting number in audit
Retain a revision on anonymised and erased records
open_points.default_guess: Require the old revision for concurrency control, then remove the revision with the rest of the erased facts.

open_points.subject: Complete failure-check order
open_points.text: A04 says “Every action checks in one order” but its six checks do not place confirmation validity, CSRF, migration closure, pending-request existence, pointer status, sign-in lockout or other operation-specific preconditions.
open_points.question: Where do all operation-specific refusal checks occur relative to the six declared checks?
options: Extend the global order with explicit additional stages
Define a per-operation ordered list after the common checks
Limit A04's order to revisioned record actions
open_points.default_guess: Limit the six-stage order to record actions and add an explicit ordered precondition list for each other operation.

open_points.subject: Project lifecycle racing pointer publication
open_points.text: A07 serializes pointer publishes and withdrawals with each other, but not with project archiving, anonymisation or deletion, although publication on an archived project must be refused.
open_points.question: Can a publish that checked an active project commit after a concurrent archive or erasure commits?
options: Serialize project lifecycle transitions with all child writes
Let an already-started publish finish
Use commit order and abort whichever violates the resulting invariant
open_points.default_guess: Serialize archiving and erasure with room and pointer writes on that project.
